item.description: The European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR) is an award-winning international think-tank that aims to conduct cutting-edge independent research on European foreign and security policy and to provide a safe meeting space for decision-makers, activists and influencers to share ideas. We build coalitions for change at the European level and promote informed debate about Europe’s role in the world. In 2007, ECFR’s founders set about creating a pan-European institution that could combine establishment credibility with intellectual insurgency. Today, ECFR remains uniquely placed to continue providing a pan-European perspective on some of the biggest strategic challenges and choices Europeans need to confront, with a network of offices in seven European capitals, over 90 staff from more than 25 different countries and a team of associated researchers in the EU 27 member states. For more information check our website: ecfr.eu

item.title: Senior Policy Advisor, Trade Diplomacy, Japan
item.description: Senior Policy Advisor, Trade Diplomacy, Japan E3G is looking for a Senior Policy Advisor to lead analysis and engagement on trade diplomacy within its Japan programme. The new role will sit within E3G’s Global Clean Power Diplomacy team and will work closely with our Japan and trade experts to develop E3G’s work on the intersection of Japan’s trade policy, energy and economic security strategies, and climate objectives – with trade playing a key role as a diplomatic lever across these areas contributing to accelerating the clean energy transition. The role The role will build on existing work on trade and its use as a diplomatic lever, leading the development of strategies and engagements to align Japan’s trade, and economic policies, with the goals of a clean energy transition and ambitious climate action. The candidate will be based in Japan and will be required to work remotely. We are looking for an intellectually curious, enthusiastic person with experience of condensing and communicating complex information into clear, targeted analysis and advice for varied stakeholders. You will be motivated by building relationships with external stakeholders, and by creating impactful outcomes through strategic collaborations. You will have the opportunity to develop the strategy and shape the work programme, in consultation with colleagues in the Japan team and across E3G’s wider trade and industry related teams. Background E3G is an independent climate change think tank with a global outlook. We are world leading strategists on the political economy of climate change, dedicated to achieving a safe climate for all. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate. Our goal is to translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. Delivering a rapid, managed transition of the global power system from coal-to-clean, not via gas, is a fundamental condition to achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement. E3G’s Global Clean Power Diplomacy team mobilises diplomatic actors to drive real-world, real-economy progress on ending the global use of the coal power and transitioning to clean energy. E3G identifies opportunities for influence and interventions, collaborates with civil society campaigns and partners, and fosters international diplomatic alliances to create a world where no new coal is built, and where existing coal is replaced by clean, affordable energy to enable a climate-safe world. Key Responsibilities Provide strategic insight and thought leadership on trade and diplomatic engagement with Japan in the context of broader global climate and energy goals. Monitor and track developments relating to Japan’s trade relationships with a focus on key partner countries, including various bilateral and multilateral frameworks and agreements (e.g. FTAs), government strategies and publications (e.g. Green Transformation Strategy; and industrial policy priorities, such as the 17 Strategic Fields under Japan’s growth strategy etc.), as well as commercial drivers relating to both traditional and clean energy supply chains, in order to assess their impact on Japan’s energy and economic security priorities and identify opportunities for strategic interventions. Produce analysis, presentations, briefings and other materials, both internally to contribute to E3Gs strategic thinking, and to a wide range of external contacts to communicate our analysis and recommendations, in both written and spoken formats. Expand E3G’s relationships and networks to relevant institutions and stakeholders in trade, energy and economic security – particularly civil society organisations (CSOs), alongside government officials, research institutions, trade associations and key private sector actors, primarily in Japan and key trade partner countries, to develop productive collaborations that support achieving the programme’s objectives. In collaboration with E3G’s Japan experts and trusted partners, maintain and widen the team’s relationships with diplomats and foreign missions and trade representatives to distribute analysis and strategic advice, for example through organising and presenting in online and in-person briefings. Represent E3G externally through active participation in civil society meetings, as well as relevant conferences and other events in Japan and internationally as needed; and maintain relations to media and provide commentary and insights about their area of expertise when needed. Experience and Skills A graduate degree in a relevant discipline, such as trade policy, international relations, climate and energy policy, development, geography, or politics. A minimum of six years of relevant professional experience in a related field, such as trade, policy, research or advocacy within a government or international organisation, commercial sector, think tank, civil society or research institute. Established connections to organisations and individuals relevant for the role, e.g. government and ministries, trade associations or related research institutions, and the ability to leverage these relationships effectively and in alignment with organisational priorities. Strong analytical and strategic thinking, with an aptitude for learning new areas and consider complex information to make evidence-based recommendations. Excellent communication skills, able to convey information and arguments to others in a clear, accessible and convincing way including in sensitive or challenging stakeholder contexts. Highly organised and attention to detail, able to be proactive and deliver high-quality outputs in a timely manner. Strong interpersonal skills, with ability to form high-trust relationships with various external stakeholders and handle sensitive information with discretion, as well as patience and resilience in long-term engagement processes. Excellent written and spoken Japanese and English. Ability to work effectively and collaboratively in an international team environment. What we offer Initial contract of one year, with possibility of extension, for a full-time position. Fully remote and flexible working arrangements. 16 vacation days + additional leave between Christmas and New Year. Eligible for social (employee health) insurance and employment insurance. E3G offers a competitive salary and reward package which compares well with other organisations within our sector, reflecting experience and qualifications of the chosen candidate. The salary shall be subject to withholdings for taxes and social and labor insurances in Japan mentioned above in which the Senior Policy Advisor will be enrolled. Yearly process for remuneration review. E3G is unable to provide relocation assistance to candidates who would need to change locations in order to take up this position. E3G will require candidates to demonstrate that they the right to live and work in Japan. How to apply Please submit your application in English. Please include: A CV of maximum two pages A cover letter of no more than one page outlining why you are applying for this role and when you would be able to start. Please include a written description of your residency status and right to work in Japan (for example, your visa status, if applicable), in the letter. The deadline for applications is Midnight, Sunday 16th August. Whilst we very much appreciate the time you will have taken with your application, unfortunately due to the level of response we receive we may not be able to reply to every candidate. Therefore, if you have not heard from us with 2 weeks of the closing date, please assume that on this occasion you have been unsuccessful. E3G values diversity and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. We aim to build an inclusive workforce that is reflective of the populations we support, and actively seek applications from those who are marginalized and underrepresented. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities.

Structure and oversee multidisciplinary workstreams, ensuring analytical rigour and delivery excellence. Lead proposal development, commercial discussions and client pitches. Establish methodologies, delivery standards and quality frameworks. Develop staffing models, capability plans and operating structures. Contribute to revenue growth and long-term sustainability of the practice. Build TBI's reputation through delivery excellence and market engagement. Thought Leadership & Public Influence Publish distinctive policy papers, market analyses and strategic commentary. Shape TBI's institutional positions on digital assets, stablecoins, tokenisation and financial infrastructure. Represent TBI at global forums, conferences and high-level policy discussions. Translate complex technical concepts into actionable insights for government leaders. Build TBI's reputation as a trusted voice in digital finance and innovation. Stakeholder & Ecosystem Engagement Design and lead flagship multi-stakeholder convenings. Build relationships across governments, central banks, regulators, fintechs, blockchain ecosystems and financial institutions. Serve as a bridge between public-sector stakeholders and industry participants. Develop strategic partnerships with multilateral organisations, industry bodies and ecosystem leaders. Internal Leadership & Capability Building Build, lead and mentor a high-performing multidisciplinary team. Develop practical frameworks, toolkits and training materials. Contribute to broader TBI leadership, strategy and talent discussions. Foster a culture of excellence, client service and continuous learning. Support capability development across TBI's global network. Person Specification Experience & Track Record 12+ years of experience spanning management consulting, public-sector advisory, financial regulation, international organisations, fintech or financial services. Demonstrated success leading high-impact advisory engagements. Strong track record of business development, proposal development and client relationship management. Experience operating in emerging markets is highly desirable. Technical & Functional Expertise Deep understanding of digital assets, stablecoins, tokenisation, CBDCs and financial infrastructure. Strong understanding of public policy, financial regulation and economic reform. Ability to lead rigorous analytical work and develop practical recommendations. Leadership & Interpersonal Skills Proven ability to lead teams and manage complex stakeholder environments. Exceptional communication and executive presence. The UNFCCC remains central to global climate action, but needs to evolve to support delivery in this new context. This means strengthening the links between negotiations and real-economy action, making greater use of coalitions and partnerships where they can deliver progress, and connecting climate diplomacy with wider economic, energy, trade, finance and development agendas. The period to the second Global Stocktake (GST2) in 2028 will be critical to demonstrating progress, building confidence in international cooperation and creating the conditions for stronger action through the next NDC cycle. We pride ourselves on bringing independence to an extremely polarised discussion and holding policy makers to account on their promises. item.description: Role Summary The Policy Advisor for AI Governance is based within the Science & Technology (S&T) Policy team in TBI’s Policy and Politics division in London. The S&T Policy team develops radical, actionable policy solutions to help governments foster innovation, accelerate technology adoption and govern emerging technologies. Artificial intelligence is developing rapidly, creating profound opportunities for economic growth and improvements in public services while raising new questions for governments about safety, security, accountability and international cooperation. Policymakers need governance approaches that can keep pace with technological change, manage emerging risks and enable societies to capture the benefits of increasingly capable AI systems. The Policy Advisor will play a central role in building and advancing TBI’s AI governance agenda. Working closely with the Director of Science & Technology Policy, they will develop ambitious and practical policy proposals for how governments should govern advanced AI. The role will have a particular focus on building effective AI assurance ecosystems , developing policy approaches to frontier open-source AI , and strengthening international coordination on AI governance . The successful candidate will combine rigorous policy analysis with excellent political judgement and exceptional written and verbal communication skills. They will be able to understand complex technical and policy questions, identify what matters for political leaders, and translate their analysis into clear, compelling and actionable recommendations. This is also an externally facing role. The Policy Advisor will represent TBI in discussions with policymakers, senior officials, technology companies, researchers and other leading voices in AI governance. They should be intellectually confident, persuasive and comfortable contributing TBI’s perspective in senior policy discussions. The role is suited to someone with established experience in AI, technology policy or a closely related field who is ready to take significant ownership of substantive policy projects while working closely with senior colleagues to shape TBI’s wider AI governance agenda. As part of your application for the Policy Advisor – AI Governance position, you are required to submit both a CV and cover letter. Your cover letter should outline your motivation for joining TBI and your interest in AI governance, including how your experience, academic background and/or expertise are relevant to the role. Please provide a cover letter explaining why you are excited to join the S&T team at TBI and why you would be good fit for this role. This is a 1 year fixed- term contract. To be considered for this opportunity, candidates must have an existing and valid right to work in the UK. Key Responsibilities The holder of this position will: Contribute to TBI’s AI governance policy agenda , working closely with Elizabeth Seger, Senior Policy Advisor - AI Governane, to identify important emerging questions, develop distinctive policy positions and translate them into actionable recommendations for governments. Lead substantial policy projects on priority AI governance issues, with a particular focus on AI assurance ecosystems, frontier open-source AI policy and international AI governance coordination. Produce outstanding written policy work , including major reports, policy papers, briefings, comment pieces and materials for senior political audiences, translating complex technical and policy questions into clear and persuasive arguments. Develop practical policy proposals that account for technological developments, institutional and regulatory constraints, political economy and the needs of policymakers implementing AI governance in practice. Provide policy advice and briefing to senior leaders within TBI and support TBI advisory teams working with governments globally, ensuring that the Institute’s work on AI governance informs practical advice to political leaders and policymakers. Track developments in AI capabilities, governance and regulation internationally , identifying emerging issues that warrant political attention and opportunities for TBI to shape policy debates. item.description: Senior Researcher, EU Industry Transition, Clean Economy, Brussels or Berlin Background E3G is a world leading strategy think tank on the political economy of climate change with a global outlook. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate for all. Our goal is to translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. We pride ourselves on bringing independence to an extremely polarised discussion and holding policy makers to account on their promises. E3G’s diplomatic work extends across the whole climate regime, including the UN negotiations and cooperation on the energy transition, financial reform, green industry, trade and increasing resilience. E3G particularly focuses on understanding and influencing the connections between climate politics and global agendas in foreign, security and economic policy. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top-ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. E3G offers a dynamic and fast paced working environment that will value your insight, initiative and collaboration wherever you are in the organisation. Role Overview The Senior Researcher will contribute to the EU Industry team’s work to accelerate the decarbonisation and transformation of European industry in line with climate neutrality, competitiveness and resilience. The role will combine policy research and analysis, political strategy, stakeholder engagement and written communications across three initial areas: reform of the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS), industrial electrification, and EU funding and support instruments. Working with colleagues across E3G, the Senior Researcher will help develop practical policy propositions, produce high-quality briefings and reports, monitor political and policy developments, and engage policymakers, civil society, business, industry, finance and other expert stakeholders. The role is suited to someone who already brings expertise in one or more relevant areas and is motivated to deepen and broaden their knowledge across the portfolio. Responsibilities Conduct research and analysis on EU industrial decarbonisation and industrial policy, initially focusing on the EU ETS, industrial electrification, and funding and investment. Develop practical policy recommendations and contribute to political strategies that support the transition of European industry. Monitor relevant EU policy and political developments, stakeholder positions and emerging debates, and translate these into timely analysis and recommendations. Produce clear, accessible briefings, reports, presentations and other materials for internal and external audiences. Engage policymakers, industry, civil society and other stakeholders, and contribute to the delivery of projects, partnerships and coalitions across E3G’s industry portfolio. Experience and Skills Three to five years of relevant professional experience, with progressively greater responsibility and a track record of delivering high-quality work. A degree, professional qualification or equivalent experience in a relevant area. Knowledge and practical experience in at least one relevant area, such as industrial decarbonisation or industrial policy; the EU ETS or carbon pricing; industrial electrification or energy policy; or EU funding, investment and support instruments. A good understanding of EU politics, institutions and policy processes. Strong research and analytical skills, including the ability to learn quickly, assess evidence and reach well-founded judgements. The ability to produce clear, accessible briefings, reports, presentations and other written materials, and to communicate ideas credibly in spoken English. Experience engaging external stakeholders and confidence working with policymakers and experts from government, civil society, business, industry and finance. Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and a focus on delivering agreed outputs, results and outcomes. Experience working in or with EU institutions, or within the Brussels policy community, and relevant stakeholder networks. Knowledge across more than one of the role’s core policy areas or of industrial sectors such as steel, cement or chemicals. Experience supporting partnerships, coalitions, consortia or multi-organisation projects. A good working knowledge of another European language. What we offer Permanent, full-time position. Flexible working arrangements and hybrid working approach. 25 vacation days + additional leave between Christmas and New Year. Employers Pension contribution plan. Yearly process for remuneration review. E3G is unable to provide any relocation assistance to candidates who would need to move in order to take up this position. Berlin The indicative salary range in Berlin is €45,990 to €47,500 annually, dependant on experience. BahnCard50 travel cover. Brussels The indicative salary range in Brussels is €3,274,10 to €3,412.40 monthly, dependant on experience, with holiday pay and a 13th month. Mobile phone and contract, lunch and eco vouchers, hospitalisation and travel insurance, travel expense reimbursement (bicycle or public transport). item.description: Role Summary TBI is seeking a Country Security Manager (CSM) for Ukraine to provide effective, proportionate, and high-quality security support to our TBI Ukraine team. The postholder will be the principal in-country security adviser, supporting the Country Director and TBI in discharging Duty of Care responsibilities through practical security risk management, preparedness, business continuity, and incident coordination. This is a locally based role in Kyiv, Ukraine. TBI is not able to sponsor, obtain or facilitate a reservation or deferment from mobilisation in connection with this position. Applicants must be able to independently meet the requirements of the position in accordance with applicable Ukrainian law and their individual mobilisation obligations. Appointment to, or employment in, this role does not alter an individual's mobilisation status or provide protection from mobilisation. Key Responsibilities Core Areas Act as the principal in-country security adviser, supporting the Country Director and TBI's Duty of Care responsibilities in Ukraine. Implement TBI's Global Duty of Care Policy and associated security requirements in Ukraine, working with Operational Capability/HQ to harmonise country arrangements with global standards. Maintain and embed the Ukraine Essential Security Package (ESP), including the Country Risk Register, Welcome Pack, SOPs, HRE Plan and contingency arrangements. Provide timely, concise and decision-focused security advice that translates developments in the operating environment into practical implications and actions for TBI. Maintain preparedness for incidents, business continuity disruption and seasonal risks, including winterisation. Build a positive security culture through staff briefings, onboarding, exercises and practical engagement. Maintain strong external security networks and coordinate specialist external support when required. Proactively escalate material risks, incidents, capability gaps and support needs to the Country Director and Operational Capability/HQ. Duty of Care, Governance and Global Standards Support the Country Director in implementing TBI's Global Duty of Care Policy and associated security requirements in Ukraine. Work closely with Operational Capability/HQ to ensure Ukraine's security arrangements remain aligned with TBI's global security standards, policies and risk-management approach. Translate global requirements into practical and proportionate country-level arrangements appropriate to the Ukrainian operating environment. Maintain effective technical coordination with Operational Capability/HQ, including escalation of material risks, incidents, capability gaps and changes in the operating environment. Participate in global security assurance, review, and quality-assurance processes as required, and implement agreed improvements. Identify where local conditions require adaptation of global approaches and work with Operational Capability/HQ to agree on appropriate solutions. Contribute lessons, emerging risks and good practice from Ukraine to the continued development of TBI's global Duty of Care and security capability. Security Continuously monitor and analyse the security context in Ukraine, with particular attention to conflict and aerial threats relevant to TBI personnel, operations and planned activity. Produce concise, timely and practical security updates for staff and leadership, clearly explaining what has changed, why it matters to TBI and whether action is required. Distinguish between general security reporting and developments that materially affect TBI's operational exposure and provide proportionate mitigation advice. Maintain and update the Ukraine Country Risk Register in accordance with TBI's global risk-management methodology. Maintain and embed the Ukraine ESP, SOPs, HRE Plan, emergency contacts and contingency arrangements, ensuring they remain aligned with global requirements. Ensure staff understand prevalent threats, security procedures, incident reporting and escalation routes, and their individual responsibilities for security. Provide proportionate security planning and advice for staff movements, programme travel, leadership visits and events, ensuring arrangements reflect the operating environment and TBI’s actual risk exposure. Build and maintain an active security network in Ukraine, including INSO, OSAC, embassy security teams, peer organisations, relevant authorities, emergency services and reputable providers. Resilience Support the Country Director and Operational Capability/HQ to maintain appropriate crisis-management, business-continuity and contingency arrangements for Ukraine. Coordinate security-related winter preparedness and monitor infrastructure disruption affecting staff, accommodation, communications, transport and office continuity. Ensure contingency plans are regularly reviewed and exercised, including HRE, evacuation, relocation and hibernation arrangements where applicable. Act as the principal in-country security focal point during incidents, coordinating initial response, staff accountability, communications and escalation. Provide timely analysis and practical options to decision-makers during incidents and support TBI crisis-management arrangements when activated. Lead or support after-action reviews and ensure lessons are incorporated into country procedures and, where relevant, shared with Operational Capability/HQ. Training and Engagement Deliver regular, practical security briefings and security onboarding for staff and visitors. Plan and deliver tabletop exercises and other proportionate security exercises to test procedures and build staff confidence. Promote a positive security culture based on shared responsibility, preparedness and practical risk awareness. Communicate security requirements in a way that is accessible, proportionate and relevant to TBI's operating environment. Representation and Coordination Act as a trusted critical friend to the Country Director and leadership, providing clear advice that enables programme delivery while appropriately managing risk. Draw on TBI resources and specialists to deliver high-quality technical advice and avoid operating as a standalone country function. Maintain strong working relationships with Operational Capability/HQ and contribute to harmonisation of Ukraine systems and practices with global standards. Coordinate specialist external capabilities, including emergency evacuation support, secure transport, or surge operational support, when required. Represent TBI professionally with internal and external stakeholders and maintain high standards of integrity, discretion and confidentiality. Role Boundaries TBI requires a lean, information-led and proportionate security capability appropriate to its operating model. This is not a close protection role. Person Specification The ideal candidate will combine strong security risk-management experience with excellent judgment, communication skills, and an understanding of how security enables an advisory organization to operate. They will be able to filter a complex security environment and provide senior leaders and staff with concise, proportionate, and practical advice. This is a role requiring an exceptional candidate: With at least five years' relevant security risk-management experience, the majority of this experience is from a volatile or conflict-affected environment. Who has a strong understanding of the legal, moral and organisational dimensions of Duty of Care and experience implementing security policy and standards at country level. Who can work effectively with HQ/global security functions to harmonise local arrangements with organisational standards while adapting them appropriately to context. Who can translate complex security information into concise, decision-focused advice for non-security audiences and senior leadership. Who has experience developing and maintaining risk assessments, security procedures, emergency arrangements and contingency plans. Who has practical experience in incident management, emergency response, and business continuity. Professionally proficient in English, both written and verbal (minimum CEFR B2 or equivalent). Candidates may be asked to demonstrate proficiency during the recruitment process. Who demonstrates excellent judgment, including the ability to distinguish between information that is interesting and information that is operationally significant. Who can work independently, make effective use of available resources and networks, and recognize when escalation or specialist support is required. Who is proactive, solution-oriented, delivery-focused, and committed to continuous improvement. Who understands and practices the importance of integrity, discretion, and confidentiality. Who is able to be based in Kyiv and fulfill the requirements of the role on an ongoing basis, taking into account applicable Ukrainian mobilization requirements. TBI cannot provide or facilitate mobilisation exemption, reservation or deferment for this position. Desirable Previous professional experience in Ukraine and a strong understanding of the Ukrainian security environment. Experience delivering security briefings, training or exercises. Existing relationships with Ukrainian and international security networks. Experience with business continuity or organisational resilience. Experience working in an international organisation, advisory organisation, consultancy, private-sector organisation or comparable professional environment. item.title: Strategic Communications Manager
item.description: Role Summary TBI comprises Policy, Politics, Advisory and Partnerships functions that all demand coherent, crisp, and politically relevant communications. In particular, we need to be pushing the debates on public policy and public services reforms, and we need to be celebrating the substantive policy work we do at TBI. To help drive this agenda we are looking to appoint a Strategic Communications Manager to our small team in London. Your number one job will be to insert TBI into the critical public policy debates where we have a unique point of view, and where the debate is decidedly antiquated or headed in the wrong direction, or even if the debate is not going far enough. We offer radical-but-practical solutions to the world’s most pressing problems and to get noticed, we need politically-savvy communicators who understand our primary audience and the media that resonates with them. We are particularly looking for someone experienced in dealing with high-profile media stories, spotting and lifting the headline-worthy material from longer thought leadership pieces, courting media, developing producers, and inserting TBI into policy debates in media and through our social channels. We also need a communicator adept at building out a strategic message calendar, consistent and inclusive of work across TBI. A current Right to Work in the UK is essential for this London-based hybrid role. Key Responsibilities Key elements of the role include: Develop media strategies for policy output as part of a wider influencing strategy for the work. Create and lead the communications, press and media strategy for elements of our policy work, ensuring we have a clear and deliverable plan to maximise our influence. Maintain strong relationships with media stakeholders, finding ways to maximise exposure opportunities for TBI’s work. Relentless in the pursuit of media coverage for our policy work and the successes of our engagements and events worldwide, making sure there is a clear headline in mind and dedicated media plan associated with every communications plan TBI develops. Maximise the effectiveness of our policy work, developing strategies that surface the key headline/message and focus the authors on how to make their work resonate with wider audiences. Work collaboratively with colleagues in social media, email marketing and content creation teams to produce multi-channel communication strategies. Use analytics and reporting tools to monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of communications and inform future activities. Act as key media advisor to TBI policy directors. Person specification The successful candidate will: Have significant experience at the nexus of policy, politics, and communications, and possess an innate understanding of the political environment in which we operate. Have strong media handling experience, preferably at the national political level in the UK, and will have dealt directly with national press and broadcast media to secure positive coverage of a high-profile agenda. Have a keen understanding of policy honed over years spent working at the coalface of decision-making and communications. Have a good ‘nose’ for the story, the political environment in which we are operating, and the social media trends that should inform our activities. Be keenly interested in the policy content of the work and willing to contribute to the thinking that goes into it. Have excellent communication skills and be able to clearly explain complex analysis and policy proposals with persuasiveness. Experience working with senior stakeholders across the organisation, confidence to influence upwards and challenge thinking at all levels. Maintain, or be able to develop, strong links to key journalists and opinion formers in the press and broadcast media. Closing Date: 2026-10-01
